# Dark Magic

*Page PDF 61*

Dark Magic 

## **Dark Magic**
## **Dark Elf Sorceresses**
Elves have a natural affinity for the shifting winds of magic. In the ancient days, they learnt the secrets of manipulating this mystical power from the slann, the most powerful servants of the Old Ones. Yet for all their expertise, there was always a limit to the amount of power the elves could harness, as the risk of madness and spiritual corruption prevented them from delving deeper into the power of Chaos. 

It was Morathi who first ventured into this forbidden territory. Through dark rituals and bloody sacrifice, she moulded the energies of Chaos to her bidding. With this sorcery, she wove enchantments whose raw power outstripped anything the elves had previously known. To this day, dark elves study the sorcerous arts, seduced by the wild energy it allows them to command. 

When Nagarythe waged war on the other realms of Ulthuan, Morathi had already corrupted many mages of Saphery. Tempted by the power of sorcery, they turned against their fellows, and a magical war raged. Eventually, they were forced to flee and sought protection and tutelage from Morathi and Malerion. 

The methods for learning dark magic are jealously guarded by sorceresses, but it is obvious that this discipline is learned at great personal cost. 

According to the _Sixth Book of Secrets_ by Kaladhtoir of Clar Karond, there are a total of twelve distinct tests that an aspirant sorceress must pass during her apprenticeship. It states: ‘ _A sorceress must walk the dark paths of the Realms of Chaos, the deep pits of the oceans, and the raging bowels of the fiery mountains in her quest for knowledge. The channelling of the raw winds of Chaos and binding of these forces give the sorceress her power. The creatures of the Chaos hells will bow down to her will in the end. Such power is vast but dangerous, and the aspirant to the Dark Convent of the Sorceresses must be courageous and strong. She must be wedded first to the Dread King, and so may never take a husband nor sire children. This also, the Dread King is alone among our fathers and forefathers able to wield the powers of the darkest abyss.’_ 

## **Male Sorcerers**
Whilst the _Sixth Book of Secrets_ suggests that Malerion is the only male able to master the art of dark magic, the claim is somewhat misleading. Dark elves of either sex can cast spell using dark magic, though male sorcerers are regarded with disdain, fear, and suspicion, and this is a situation only exacerbated by the generous bounties Malerion offers in return for their severed heads. 

Tales are told of the Prophecy of Demise, uttered by Caledor following a vision he received whilst Aenarion drew forth the Widowmaker at the Shrine of Khaine.
